subject: templated arguments: T vs. const T&

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: templated arguments: T vs. const T&
parts:
[moved to stan-dev]

On 5/25/13 5:12 PM, Marco Inacio wrote:
> Thanks, I've fixed the formatting issues you pointed. Also, is there any special reason for some (a lot) of functions be
> defined as log1p(const T x) { } instead of log1p(const T& x) { }. I could also include this in the patch, but maybe the
> compiler automatically optimizes this, though.

The right thing to do for a templated argument is:

T: only arithmetic types (double, float, int, long, size_t, etc.)

const T&: class types (var, fvar, etc.)

If you're going to instantiate with both, use the const reference.

- Bob

Anything that involves run-time indirection is going to be
slower.

Inlined const references can often be optimized away.
But "inline" is only a suggestion. Compilers vary and a single
compiler will vary by optimization level and other settings.

owens_t has only var specialization. For this one it seems at first that
fvar would be good since the derivative is kind of huge.
